overview.oneLineTake: Hot CPI plus an AI unwind forced the first serious equity flush since July; vol sellers face a rates-and-credit twin risk into the next data prints.
themes: Hot September CPI at 3.7% year on year, led by gasoline, lifted Fed hike odds, and Goolsbee said more bad inflation prints would be unacceptable.
Risk-off tape: SPY closed at 769.60 (-1.1%) and QQQ at 728.95 (-2.0%), the first -1% S&P 500 and -2% Nasdaq 100 day since late July.
The AI complex cracked: Dell led data-center selling, CoreWeave bonds traded near distressed levels, and chip and infrastructure names extended losses into the close.
Energy and geopolitics keep fuel sticky, with Hormuz disruptions, a diesel squeeze into 2027 and noise around the disputed Russia diesel deal.
Bank earnings were mixed: Morgan Stanley beat on equities while BofA missed and took a $1.2B charge, and Dimon warned on inflation and under-the-surface risks.
risks: Rate-hike repricing if energy-driven CPI stays sticky into the midterms.
AI credit stress at CoreWeave and other neoclouds spilling into broader risk appetite.
Overnight futures still soft (ES -0.2%, NQ -0.5%) after the Oct 14 washout.

nq.overnight: NQ 29,886, under the 30,155 open and near the 29,880 overnight low (high 30,158). Squawk has Nasdaq futures around -0.5%.
nq.macro: Goolsbee said more bad inflation months would be unacceptable, and hike odds rose after the 3.7% CPI. 10Y 5.19%, DXY 102.2.
nq.volatility: VIX 16.9 (+10.5%) off the flush, still not panic. VXN 21.1. Dealer gamma unavailable.

intelligence.headline: The Former Theater Director Who Keeps Beating Wall Street
intelligence.summary: Brian Golden, a 44-year-old former theater director, is the most successful trader in Kalshi economic markets with over $2 million in profits, and over the last 18 CPI reports none of the 25 bank economists tracked by Bloomberg beat his forecast accuracy. For this morning's reading he expects 3.66% year on year, just above the 3.6% consensus.

intelligence.headline: US Stocks Poised to Open Modestly Higher
intelligence.summary: US stocks were set to open modestly higher as investors look ahead to an inflation reading and another round of bank earnings.

intelligence.headline: Fed's Williams Currently Sees No Need for Rate Hike in 2027
intelligence.summary: New York Fed chief John Williams says one more interest-rate increase is appropriate this year, but he does not currently see a need to hike in 2027.

intelligence.headline: BofA Hit With $1.2 Billion of Fines Over Money Laundering Lapses
intelligence.summary: Bank of America, which reports earnings this morning, was fined more than $1.2 billion for money laundering and sanctions violations, and the stock slid 1.8%.

intelligence.headline: Aramco Headquarters Hit as Houthis Widen Attacks on Saudi Arabia
intelligence.summary: Aramco offices were hit as Iran-backed Houthis launched attacks across Saudi Arabia, and oil ticked higher; Brent was $105.40 (-0.3%) in the snapshot.

intelligence.headline: ASML Raises Full-Year Sales Outlook as AI Boom Drives Demand
intelligence.summary: ASML shares rose after the company said it can't keep up with AI demand.

intelligence.headline: Bond Traders Eclipsed by Equities in Rare Wall Street Reversal
intelligence.summary: Equities divisions at five big US banks are on track for more than $66 billion of revenue in the first nine months, roughly $3 billion above bond, currency and commodity units, with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley reporting today.

intelligence.headline: ECB Will Probably Have to Hike Interest Rates Again, Wunsch Says
intelligence.summary: ECB Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch said "We are probably going to have to hike again" as the ECB debates adding to two hikes this year with inflation approaching 4%, with Middle East fighting and France's fiscal crisis likely key factors.

intelligence.headline: IMF Says US Growth Not Enough to Fight High Debt, Deficit Levels
intelligence.summary: US GDP needs to grow roughly 6% a year to stabilize government debt, and the IMF head said Scott Bessent's plan to grow out of the debt problem won't work fast enough.
